children: shares fell about 2% Tuesday after HSBC lowered its view on the streaming company, pointing to growing competition from YouTube and weaker signs of viewer engagement, according to a Tuesday analyst note.

HSBC analyst Mohammed Khallouf cut Netflix to Hold from Buy and reduced his price target to $76 from $96. The revised target reflects a 21% reduction and leaves limited room for gains based on Tuesday's trading level.

The analyst said YouTube is capturing more television viewing while Netflix faces challenges keeping its original programming compelling to audiences. YouTube is also expanding its appeal to creators through financial incentives and marketing support, potentially making the competition for exclusive content more difficult.

HSBC also pointed to changes in YouTube's product design that bring elements of traditional episodic television into the platform. Meanwhile, Netflix's recent awards performance and audience reception for some franchise releases have raised questions about the strength of its content lineup.

Khallouf said weaker engagement could affect subscriber retention, pricing flexibility and advertising appeal. He expects those pressures to remain a concern in the near term as Netflix competes for viewer attention.

title: Netflix Stock Drops on HSBC Downgrade, Citing YouTube Threat
